subject: Discovery recap - Reliability & graceful degradation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elisa Ramos <elisa.ramos@fintechco.com>, Amit Patel <amit.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap - Reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Elisa / Amit —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Top pain points you shared:
- Recent multi-hour outage last quarter due to provider-side network partitioning; secondary failover didn’t activate cleanly.
- High tail latency from your current in-house LLM endpoints during peak batch jobs (95th/99th spikes).
- Lack of deterministic fallbacks: when primary models/regions are degraded, the system currently returns errors rather than degraded-but-useful responses.

Current stack (as described):
- Primary: in-house GPU cluster (K8s-managed endpoints) + S3 for artifacts.
- Secondary: limited cross-region replicas; some traffic sent to cloud vendor A but no automatic model variant fallback.
- Observability: Datadog for infra, but model-level token latency and cost breakdowns are sparse.

Success criteria for a pilot / evaluation:
1) No user-impacting outages for inference layer under our defined load profile (30k qps bursts) — target 99.9% availability during pilot.
2) Controlled graceful degradation: when capacity constrained, responses should fallback to smaller quantized models (or cached summaries) instead of errors, with clear SLAs on correctness for core flows.
3) Measurable unit cost reduction of at least 25% vs current per-token cost under typical workload.
4) Security/compliance gate: SOC2 audit evidence and VPC deployment option for production.

Incident history notes you gave:
- June 2026: DNS flapping led to 3.5 hrs of failed inference for internal customers.
- Aug 2026: Large batch job caused GPU OOMs and cascading queue buildup — 2 hours degraded performance.

Our proposed mitigations (high level):
- Multi-tier fallbacks: primary model -> quantized variant -> cached prefix summaries -> lightweight rule-based fallback for critical flows.
- Smart routing by policy: latency-first for user-facing traffic, cost-first for background batch jobs.
- Cross-region model replicas with automatic region failover and controlled cold-start prewarming for critical paths.
- Observability: token-level traces, per-model SLO dashboards, and breakpoint alerts tied to user-visible errors.

Next steps (agreed):
1) I’ll share a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a proposed pilot scope + success metrics (attached).
2) Elisa / Amit: confirm procurement timeline and any additional security docs you need (e.g., contact for SOC2 evidence).
3) Schedule a 60-min pilot design call next week to nail the traffic shape, models for fallback, and rollout policy.

Attachments: rdw-map-proposal.pdf (pilot scope + MAP)

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Elisa Ramos <elisa.ramos@fintechco.com>

Cc: Amit Patel <amit.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - Reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Ben —

This is a great summary, thank you. A few clarifications / additional context from our side:
- The June outage was exacerbated because our traffic routing rules didn’t trigger failover until error thresholds were already exceeded; we want more conservative failover thresholds.
- For success criteria #2, we’d like call-level guarantees for important customer-facing endpoints (payments and customer-verification flows). Can you map what graceful-degradation options preserve payment flow integrity (e.g., cached KYC summaries vs partial model responses)?
- Procurement: we’re targeting a PO by end of November; security sign-off is the gating item. I’ll loop in our procurement lead once we confirm the MAP.

A couple of asks before the pilot design call:
1) Can you send a sample SLO/SLA template for inference (availability, P95/P99 latency, error budget policy)?
2) Have you run similar graceful-degradation playbooks for finance customers? Any case studies or short notes would help our security team.

I’ve copied Amit (infra) — Amit, can you share the rough steady-state qps we should plan for and the peak burst shapes?

Best,
Elisa Ramos
Head of Platform Reliability | FinTechCo
